title: Recording, mixing: Give Ireland Back To The Irish by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, Island Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Brian Humphries

The second and final recording session for Wings’ debut single ‘Give Ireland Back To The Irish’ took place on 3 February 1972.

The song had been written on 31 January, and the backing track had been recorded on 1 February at EMI Studios. However, it remained unfinished by the 5.30am end of the session.

Two days later Wings completed the song at Island Studios in Notting Hill, London. Paul McCartney and Henry McCullough overdubbed arpeggiated electric guitar parts, and they, along with Denny Laine and Denny Seiwell, added penny whistles.

The latter was for an instrumental version. This was inspired by the McCartneys’ recent Jamaican holiday, where they found reggae singles with instrumental b-sides. Doing so had an added bonus: if the political single proved too much for radio stations to offer airplay, they could play the flipside instead.

The final overdub was the sound of marching feet. It was achieved by a bucket of gravel being scattered over the studio floor, over which the members of Wings were recorded marching.

The song was mixed early the following morning by studio engineer Brian Humphries, with the session ending at 7am. Humphries then took the master tapes to George Peckham at Apple Studios to be mastered for single release.

Page last updated: 19 November 2025
